controlName: Risk Treatments, Response, Recovery, and Communication Plans
purpose: Ensures the organization has documented, regularly monitored plans for how it will respond to, recover from, and communicate about AI risk events — not just a theoretical incident response policy that's never been exercised.
summary: Risk treatments, including response and recovery, and communication plans for the identified and measured AI risks are documented and monitored regularly, including post-deployment monitoring for anticipated and unanticipated impacts, response and recovery from AI incidents, and mechanisms for communicating incidents to affected stakeholders.
expectedStatementElements: How post-deployment monitoring tracks both anticipated and unanticipated impacts
What the documented incident response and recovery process looks like for AI-specific incidents
How and to whom incidents are communicated once they occur, including affected stakeholders
How often risk treatment plans are reviewed and updated based on new information
evidenceExamples: Post-deployment monitoring plan covering both expected and unexpected impacts
AI incident response and recovery procedure documentation
Stakeholder communication plan or template for AI incidents
Review history showing risk treatment plans have been updated over time
commonGaps: Post-deployment monitoring only tracks metrics the team expected to see, missing unanticipated impacts
Incident response plans exist for general IT but nothing AI-specific
No plan exists for communicating an AI incident to affected external stakeholders
Risk treatment plans were written once and never revisited as circumstances changed
interviewQuestions: How would you catch an impact from this AI system that nobody anticipated in advance?
Walk me through your incident response process specifically for an AI-related incident.
If this AI system caused harm to an external user, how would that be communicated to them?
When was your risk treatment plan for this system last reviewed and updated?
